title: प्रयोग सापेक्षमा भाषाको अस्तित्व
nepali: मानिससँग भाषाको अभेद्य सम्बन्ध छ । भाषाको गति वा अस्तित्व मानिसको भाषिक व्यवहारमा आधारित हुन्छ । भाषाको अस्तित्वका सवालमा सचेतवर्ग विशेष संवेदनशील बन्नु आवश्यक छ । यस लेखको मूल उद्देश्य भाषाको अस्तित्व, जीवन तथा मृत्युका सन्दर्भमा सैद्धान्तिक स्वरूप उल्लेख गर्दै तिनको पुस्ट्याईँका लागि तथ्यपरक उदाहरणसमेत प्रस्तुत गर्नु हो । यो लेख पूर्णतः गुणात्मक ढाँचामा तयार पारिएको छ । यसमा भाषाको अस्तित्वसँग सम्बद्ध भाषिक अवलम्बन, भाषिक स्वीकरण, भाषिक अपक्षय, भाषिक मृत्युका बारेमा चर्चा गरिएका सैद्धान्तिक ग्रन्थ एवम् तीन जना भिन्न भाषीसँग गरिएको संवादलाई प्रमुख स्रोत सामग्री बनाइएको छ । विश्वका अधिकांश भाषाहरू जस्तै नेपालका अधिकांश भाषाहरूको पनि पहिचान र अस्तित्व सङ्कटोन्मुख छ । नेपालका सबै राष्ट्रभाषालाई समाज तथा समुदायले विशेष पहिचान दिने र राज्यका विभिन्न संरचनाबाट त्यस्ता भाषाको संरक्षण एवम् प्रवर्धनमा विशेष कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता रहेको छ । प्रत्येक मातृभाषी आआफ्ना भाषाको अवलम्बन गर्दै अन्य भाषाको अनावश्यक स्वीकरणको दिशाबाट विमुख हुन सकेमा मात्र नेपालका कुनै पनि भाषा मृत्युको मुखमा पर्दैनन् र सबै भाषाको संरक्षण एवम् प्रवर्धन हुने सम्भावना रहन्छ । तसर्थ प्रत्येक भाषाका मूल वक्ताहरूले आआफ्नै भाषाका माध्यमबाट भाषिक व्यवहार गर्दै आआफ्ना भाषाप्रति सचेततापूर्वक समर्पित हुनु आवश्यक छ । साथै, यस सवालमा राज्यसंयन्त्र, अनुसन्धाता एवम् प्राज्ञिक व्यक्तित्वहरूको पनि प्रमुख भूमिका हुने भएकाले संवेदनशील बन्नु आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।
american_english: Man has an inseparable relationship with language. The vitality or existence of language is based on man's linguistic behavior. In matters of the existence of language, the conscious class must be especially sensitive. The main objective of this article is to mention the theoretical form of the existence, life and death of language and to present factual examples in support of them. This article has been prepared entirely in a qualitative framework. In it, theoretical works discussing linguistic adoption, linguistic acceptance, linguistic decay and language death in connection with the existence of language, as well as a dialogue held with three speakers of different languages, have been made the main source material. Just as most languages of the world, most languages of Nepal are also endangered in their identity and existence. There is a need for society and community to give special recognition to all national languages of Nepal and for special programs to be run from various structures of the state for the protection and promotion of such languages. Only if every mother-tongue speaker adopts his or her own language and turns away from the direction of unnecessary acceptance of other languages will no language of Nepal fall into the jaws of death, and there will remain the possibility of the protection and promotion of all languages. Therefore, it is necessary for the native speakers of each language to engage in linguistic behavior through their own language and to become consciously devoted to their own language. In addition, since the state apparatus, researchers and academic personalities also have a major role in this matter, it appears necessary to be sensitive.

informal_english: People have an inseparable bond with language. The life or existence of language rests on how people actually use it. When it comes to language's existence, the switched-on crowd really needs to be tuned in. The main aim of this article is to lay out the theory around language's existence, life and death, and back it up with real examples. The whole thing's written in a qualitative framework. It draws on theoretical works that talk about linguistic adoption, acceptance, decay and language death, plus a chat with three speakers of different languages, as the main source material. Like most languages around the world, most of Nepal's languages are under threat in their identity and existence. There's a real need for society and community to give all of Nepal's national languages special recognition, and for the state to run special programmes through its various structures to protect and promote them. Only if every mother-tongue speaker sticks with their own language and steers clear of unnecessarily taking on other languages will no Nepali language end up on death's door, and there'll be a chance for all languages to be protected and promoted. So it's necessary for the native speakers of each language to use their own language in everyday linguistic practice and to be consciously committed to it. On top of that, since the state machinery, researchers and academic types also have a big role to play here, it seems necessary for them to be tuned in too.
